jobs.title: 3L Student Practice Act Intern at Arapahoe County Government
jobs.description: Employer: Arapahoe County Government Expires: 09/21/2026 The Arapahoe County government serves its communities in ways both obvious and obscure. As the beating heart of local and regional government, we’re here for our neighbors on their best days—and their worst. We share our residents’ goals of preserving our quality of life and strive to be the place we’re proud to call home. GENERAL DESCRIPTION OF JOB:The 3L Student Practice Act (SPA) Internship Program receives law student applicants who will have completed two full years of law school prior to their internship start date. The SPA internship program is the first step towards a career as a prosecutor within the DA’s Office. Unparalleled ExperienceOur SPA Internship program provides hands-on courtroom experience in the prosecution of criminal cases under supervision. Interns appear in court to argue motions and sentencing matters, conduct jury trials, and negotiate plea dispositions with defense counsel and self-represented defendants. Responsibilities include participation in all phases of trial practice, including voir dire, opening and closing statements, and direct and cross-examinations. In addition, interns review active criminal cases, consult with victims, and negotiate plea offers, with full-year interns typically conducting an average of 13 jury trials prior to licensureFuture InvestmentUpon completion of the SPA internship program in May, we look to extend job offers to deserving interns prior to taking and passing the bar. Unlike many other offices, we do not wait until after bar results to offer employment to deserving interns. Once these SPA interns who have been offered employment take and pass the bar, they have a job waiting for them. In the past 6 years, 92% of interns who completed a year in our SPA internship program were offered a job with our office before they graduated law school.TrainingWe designed our SPA internship program to equip our interns with the skills and knowledge to seamlessly step into a full criminal caseload and try jury trials solo the day they pass the bar. In addition to the extensive experience each SPA intern gets handling real criminal cases, we provide weekly trainings, daily guidance and supervision from deputy district attorneys in the courtroom, and one-to-one mentorship from the County Court Chief Deputy District Attorney. Our Chiefs are seasoned trial attorneys, experienced in handling some of the highest profile cases in the state, and versed in cutting edge trial presentation and technology.Part of Our TeamOur SPA interns are NOT an afterthought, crammed together into a cubicle, using shared computers, and excluded from opportunities afforded deputy district attorneys. Our SPA interns are an integral part our team and we treat them as such. They get an office, a laptop, and join in with county court deputy district attorneys for meetings, trainings, and gatherings. DUTIES:Under the supervision of licensed deputy district attorneys, interns handle a docket of either or both traffic and misdemeanor cases. This includes initial and on-going case review (including to ensure provability and to ensure information is properly made available to the defense), follow-up with law enforcement agencies, negotiations with defense counsel, meeting with witnesses and victims, motions and trial. Issues arising out of county court (traffic and misdemeanor cases) are briefed in the District Court. Deputies spend a considerable amount of time in court and professional judgment is critical. This includes but is not limited to trying cases and establishing that elements of a crime have been proven beyond a reasonable doubt. Trials consist of jury selection, opening statements, direct and cross examination of witnesses, and closing arguments. Interns are expected to demonstrate appropriate demeanor and professionalism in court. Interns research and respond to a wide variety of defense motions, including motions for the suppression of evidence. This also involves preparing motions on behalf of the People. REQUIREMENTS:Skills, Abilities and Competencies:Ability to advocate legal and factual scenarios in a clear and persuasive manner to judges and jurors.Ability to rapidly assess cases for strengths versus weaknesses and aggravators versus mitigators to determine just and ethical dispositions that are within policies promulgated by the District Attorney.Ability to recognize situations warranting potential policy/procedure exceptions, and the ability to effectively advocate for alternative resolutions.Ability to react quickly and appropriately in court to defense objections, oral motions, court inquiries and rulings, and presentations/responses from defense attorneys and witnesses.This position involves the ability to effectively process and dispose of a high volume of criminal case filings while maintaining a balance of equal justice between victims, the People of the State of Colorado, and affected defendants.Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with superiors, co-workers, defense attorneys, prose defendants, victims, witnesses, judges, court staff, law enforcement and related agencies' personnel, press/media Behavioral Competencies (these are required for all positions at ACG): AccountabilityAccessibilityInclusivityIntegrityEducation and Experience: Candidates are required to currently be attending law school and must be qualified to practice under the student practice act prior to starting the 3L Student Practice Act Internship. See C.R.C.P. Rule 205.7.Experience: None Supplemental InformationTimeline for application:We accept applications and hire interns for the 3L Student Practice Act Internship Program beginning in December of a student’s second year in law school for a spot in the Internship Program for the following Summer semester (when the student becomes eligible under the student practice act). We continue to accept applications throughout the second and third year of law school. For students attending a law school not in Colorado and who desire to work in Colorado as a prosecutor after graduation, we also accept applications for the summer semester only. Pre-Employment Additional Requirements:Must successfully pass pre-employment testing which includes an acceptable motor vehicle record (MVR) and background check.Possession of a valid Class “R” Colorado Driver’s License or the ability to obtain one within two weeks of appointment.Security clearance required: will require fingerprinting and a Colorado Bureau of Investigation (CBI) background check WORK ENVIRONMENT:Work is generally confined to a standard office environment.During the summer semester, 3L Student Practice Act Interns work 35 hours per week. During the fall and spring semester, 3L Student Practice Act Interns work 8 hours a day, 2 or 3 days a week. Accommodations to this schedule can be made, however. Please list and discuss any accommodations required during your interview.PHYSICAL DEMANDS:Spends 90% of the time sitting and 10% of the time either standing or walking.Occasionally lifts, carries, pulls or pushes up to 20 lbs.Occasionally uses cart, dolly, or other equipment to carry in excess of 20 lbs.Occasionally climbs, stoops, kneels, balances, reaches, crawls and crouches while performing office or work duties.Verbal and auditory capacity enabling constant interpersonal communication through automated devices, such as telephones, radios, and similar; and in public meetings and personal interactions.Constant use of eye, hand and finger coordination enabling the use of automated office machinery or equipment.Visual capacity enabling constant use of computer or other work-related equipment. Definitions:Occasionally: Activity exists less than 1/3 of the time.Frequently: Activity exists between 1/3 and 2/3 of the time.Constantly: Activity exists more than 2/3 of the time. ** Arapahoe County does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability, genetic information, sexual orientation or any other status protected under the law. It is our intention that all qualified applicants be given equal opportunity in any term, condition, or privilege of employment and that selection decisions are based on job-related factors. Arapahoe County is committed to making employment accessible to persons with disabilities. ** In accordance with Senate Bill 23-058, applicants understand that Arapahoe County will not request or require the applicant to include their age, date of birth, or date of attendance/graduation date on the initial application. Applicants understand that Arapahoe County can request or require an individual to provide documentation including copies of certification, transcripts, and other materials created by a third party. The applicant understands that the applicant can redact, if they so choose, information that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance/graduation from an educational institution on those requested/required certification, transcripts and other materials created by a third party.

jobs.description: Employer: Sacramento State: SSAE Expires: 09/22/2026 Esak’timá Native Student Resource Center Graduate Advisor Internship WHAT IS THE ESAK’TIMÁ NATIVE STUDENT RESOURCE CENTER?The Esak’timá Native Student Resource Center serves all Sacramento State community members and allies regardless of race, sex, color, ethnicity or national origin, who are interested in Native culture, heritage, and life. Across Sacramento State and in the community, the Center is committed to holding space to cultivate collaboration to address the unique and diverse needs of Native students and issues impacting these communities. The Esak’timá Native Student Resource Center provides supportive services for students to assist them in their academic journey with Academic Advising, Academic Workshops, Peer Advising, Scholarship referrals, Cultural Presentations and Workshops, Student Leadership opportunities and Campus and Community Resources. We strive to make the Esak’timá Native Student Resource Center a home away from home where Native American values as a student are recognized, their student accomplishments are celebrated and their contributions to our community are honored. The Center is an open and inclusive gathering space for all students. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: •Graduate student at Sacramento State with a minimum 3.0. GPA in Counselor Education, Social Work, Educational Leadership and Policy Studies or any other related discipline.•Demonstrated general knowledge of the unique traits found among Native American/Alaska Native, first-generation college students and the desire to work with students from diverse backgrounds •Experience advising students in academics, leadership development, student service support areas, and CSU graduation requirements is a plus •Ability to work independently and in a group setting in addition to coordinating many different tasks.•Excellent written and verbal communication skills, professional etiquette, and interpersonal skills•Demonstrated familiarity with Microsoft Office and internet research engines. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Under the direct supervision of the Director, the Graduate Intern will be responsible for the following:•Conducting mentoring and advising sessions with program students•Facilitate workshops for all program students. Potential topics of discussion include: self-exploration, decision-making and goal setting, graduate school, studying abroad, scholarship application filing, leadership development, etc. •Help with student development concerns with the supervision of a lead counselor•Hold individual office hours and advising sessions on a weekly basis to assist students•Assist the Center staff with program planning aspects related to university life •Provide academic advising and create general education plans with students and assist with class schedule planning and registration •Attend weekly Esak’timá Native Student Resource Center retention meetings to ensure the success of Native students. TYPICAL WORKING CONDITIONS: •Interns should be available to work a minimum of 12 hours per week between 8:00 am - 5:00 pm M-F. •The minimum work periods are in 4-hour blocks of time. •The internship is a one academic year commitment.•The work is performed in an office environment with continuous contact with students, staff, the campus community, the public, and other agencies. OTHER DUTIES AS ASSIGNED• Interns will be expected to assist Esak’timá Native Student Resource Center during program events, activities and conferences.• Assist the Assistant Vice President of Student and other Staff with other duties as requested.

jobs.description: Employer: Camp Bear Creek Expires: 10/02/2026 Cabin Counselor – Summer StaffLocation: Camp Bear Creek – Eastern IowaWebsite: https://bearcreek.camp/current-job-openings/summer-camp/Dates: May 23-July 24, 2027Being a Cabin Counselor is exhausting. It’s messy. It’s challenging. And it’s also one of the most rewarding things you can do with your summer.Camp Bear Creek is a Christian summer camp in Eastern Iowa serving kids from kindergarten through 12th grade. We’re looking for passionate, fun, dedicated people who want to spend a summer making a real difference — in the lives of campers and in their own.What We’re Looking For:We want people who:Love working with kidsCan serve as strong, positive role modelsAre ready to lead Are excited to help young people grow in faithDon’t mind unplugging and spending a summer in the woodsWe aren't going to lie, being a camp counselor is incredibly hard work. You’ll be responsible for the daily care and well-being of the campers in your cabin — making sure they eat, sleep, brush their teeth, wear socks, and feel safe. It looks different each week and could mean sitting up with them at night when they're scared of the dark. It means teaching them how to paddle a kayak, supporting them at the rock wall/zip lines, building fires for skillet enchiladas (you’re going to love it), dancing to Grooveship worship and answering their questions about Jesus in Bible It also means picking up a kid when they fall in the dirt, giving them a high five when they finally hit the bullseye in archery, and letting them cover you in mud in the creek. It's all part of walking alongside campers through a week of fun, growth, and faith—and helping give them a summer they'll never forget.At Camp Bear Creek, counselors don’t just supervise- they lead. You’ll gain real world experience in:Leadership and public speakingCurriculum planning and facilitationConflict resolution and creative problem-solving Teamwork across diverse backgrounds. These soft skills are essential in every career field. You’ll also lead a variety of camp activities and work with different age groups- giving you the opportunity to grow into a well-rounded leader. We are also willing to work with you to ensure that this job can be used for internship credit in fields like Education, Public Health, Recreation & Leisure, Youth Services, Psychology and more. However, any student in any field can benefit from a summer camp experience like this. You’ll be part of an incredible team of about 30 college-aged staff from across Iowa, the U.S., and even around the world. We work hard. We play hard. We show up for each other every day. You’ll be surrounded by people who push you to grow — and who feel like family by the end of week one. This is more than a job. It’s a ministry, a leadership opportunity, and a summer you’ll never forget. You’ll give this job everything you’ve got — and it will give even more back.So, if you're looking for a summer full of purpose, adventure, community, and growth, don't let this opportunity pass you by. For more information about working at Camp Bear Creek or to apply, visit https://bearcreek.camp/current-job-openings/summer-camp/

Interns will also develop and implement programs for campers which they will lead during Winter Camp (February 22-26), Spring Camp (April 26-30), and/or Summer Camp (June 21-August 27). We ask that interns complete at least one project of their choice during their term that will support our mission, examples of some project ideas can be found below but should be based on the intern’s interests and organization’s needs. Interns must also present some sort of culmination of their internship experience and projects to the staff of Prescott Farm. The exact details of the presentation can be worked out depending on the projects they complete and the intern’s interests.During camp, interns work 36-40 hours Monday through Friday, typically 8:30am to 4:30pm, with the exception of 3-4 shifts of extended care coverage per week (the before care shift starts at 7:45am and the after care shift ends at 5pm). Interns will be paired with another intern or camp instructor and together they will be assigned a group of up to 12 campers. They are responsible for daily supervision and instruction of their campers as well as the larger camp community ages 5-14. Interns will develop programs and activities for campers and lead them through their day. Activity topics may include but are not limited to environmental science, plant and animal ID, natural exploration of the forest, fields, and wetlands, fire-making, cooking, gardening, shelter-building, and teambuilding. We ask interns to prioritize teaching hands-on, outdoor programs that encourage exploration of and care for our natural environment and wildlife.This position is in-person in Laconia, NH and interns must have access to a personal vehicle in order to commute to and from work (there is no reliable public transportation in the area). Housing is not provided. Responsibilities:Lead educational experiences on- and off-site to children ages 5-18 and occasionally adultsComplete at least one project that supports Prescott Farm’s mission (examples below)Maintain safe, kind, proactive, and inclusive behavior management strategies with childrenArrive on time for all scheduled days and stay for the entire duration of your scheduled timeCommunicate any anticipated and emergency time off in a timely manner with the Camp DirectorUse the Prescott Farm 2-way radios to communicate with other staff members during the dayShare in maintenance of program equipmentOccasionally assist with preschool age students with preschool teachers presentOther duties as assignedAdditional Responsibilities During Camp:Supervise campers and maintain safe practices, upholding all WildQuest Camp policies Develop and lead programs and activities for campers on a variety of science and nature topics to groups of up to12 campers (ages 5-14), sometimes with a co-instructor and sometimes independentlyLead campers in hands-on activities related to the camp themes as well as teambuilding activities, games, and songsEmploy inquiry-based teaching methods to stimulate learningHelp build a sense of community among campers and encourage positive interactions and self-esteem of campersBe a role model for campers by being kind and courteous to all members of the camp community and by being properly prepared for the day’s weather, including wearing the appropriate gearParticipate in, facilitate, and encourage positive, productive interactions between campers, Volunteer Junior Instructors, and fellow interns and staff membersParticipate in camp staff meetings at the beginning and end of each dayCommunicate camper health and behavior concerns with the Camp DirectorDocument accidents and incidents in a timely and appropriate mannerParticipate in working AM and PM extended care coverage on a rotating scheduleEnhance existing curriculum with creative and thought-provoking ideas and activitiesTake initiative in problem-solving, fostering effective interaction between campers, staff, and parentsOther duties as assigned Project Examples:Create signage, social media, or blog posts providing educational interpretation of a natural aspect of our locationCreate signage, social media, or blog posts providing interpretation of a historical aspect of our locationCreate a natural interpretative display for the education center lobbyIdentify, plan, and implement ways to improve trail sustainability (ex/ stepping stones in wet areas)Create and implement a story walk experience on-site for visitorsExpand our community science options for volunteersOther projects available depending on intern’s interests and organization’s needs Work Environment:Activities take place throughout our 160-acre property with over 3 miles of trails through woods and fields. Trail and other program areas may be rocky, wet, muddy, buggy, or sloped. Unless safety is a severe concern (such as thunderstorms), we live by the saying, “There’s no bad weather, only bad gear.”Interns may work with domesticated animals such as chickens, a rabbit, a turtle, and honeybees (direct interaction with the honeybees will be limited to staff with proper training, comfort, and safety gear).Staff will also encounter wild animals which may include insects, snakes, frogs, spiders, salamanders, and native mammals. Interns are also encouraged to provide feedback as a means of enhancing the internship program experience.While working at camp, interns should have their cellphones accessible for emergencies but cell phones should be out of sight when campers and their families are present. The camp office and main Prescott Farm office will both be available for staff to use for computer, cell phone, and other internet needs. Qualifications:An individual who is at least 18 years oldAn interest in working with children. Previous camp or teaching experience is desirable but not required.Ability to maintain safety and manage a group of children in a fun and positive way.Must be willing to follow all Prescott Farm health and safety rules.Ability to model responsible behavior to program participants while sharing a sincere interest in the natural and environmental sciences, outdoor skills, and education. jobs.title: Underwriting Summer Intern at Odyssey Group
jobs.description: Employer: Odyssey Group Expires: 10/09/2026 2027 Summer Intern, UnderwritingThe CompanyOdysseyRe is the reinsurance arm of the Odyssey Group, a global insurance and reinsurance enterprise wholly owned by Fairfax Financial Holdings Limited. OdysseyRe offers a broad range of property, casualty, and specialty reinsurance solutions through a network of branch and representative offices around the world. OdysseyRe’s Underwriting Division evaluates insurance risks on both a portfolio basis (Treaty reinsurance) and an individual risk basis (Facultative reinsurance). The principal responsibilities of an underwriter are to conduct an in-depth review of a Treaty or Facultative business opportunity by reviewing data and other relevant documents, determining the level of risk, and ultimately deciding if OdysseyRe should support the deal. Underwriters are client-facing and represent OdysseyRe in the market, working closely with reinsurance brokers and insurance company clients to negotiate transactions. In coordination with other departments to evaluate reinsurance opportunities, underwriters are the key revenue generators and the decisions they make are key to the Company’s performance. The OpportunityOdysseyRe’s Underwriting Internship Program is a 10-week rotational program offering a unique perspective of the reinsurance industry. As an intern, you will rotate through several underwriting divisions (Property Treaty, Casualty Treaty, Casualty Facultative, Accident and Health, etc.) to learn reinsurance basics, the day-to-day responsibilities of an underwriter, and the intricacies of each market. These foundational experiences will develop your technical skills and provide you with an understanding of our underwriting philosophy, which will endow you with the necessary skills to help underwrite new and renewal business. Several projects will be assigned during your rotations and the program will culminate with a presentation to senior management outlining your overall experience. If you are eager to learn and possess strong interpersonal skills, this is the role for you. You will engage with senior leaders daily and build your network at a variety industry events over the course of the summer. QualificationsThe Underwriting Internship Program is open to highly motivated students who are in their junior year of an undergraduate program and meet the following criteria: GPA 3.2 and aboveExceptional presentation and communication skills, both verbal and written Excellent interpersonal skillsAnalytical thinker with strong attention to detailDemonstrated leadership abilities through college or community activitiesTeam-oriented with the ability to work independently This is a hybrid role requiring 4 days in-office and 1 day remote each week, based out of our Stamford, CT office with occasional travel to New York City (approximately 20% of the time). #LI-Hybrid

jobs.title: 2027 Resource Planning and Biometrics Internship at American Forest Management
jobs.description: Employer: American Forest Management Expires: 10/09/2026 American Forest Management (AFM) is seeking a motivated and curious Resource Planning and Biometrics Intern to join the Resource Planning and Biometric Services (RPBS) group at AFM. RPBS is responsible for providing forest planning services which support client land management and forest investment decisions, as well as biometric services necessary for planning projections, inventory analysis, and data systems. Primary Duties and Responsibilities:Apply advanced analytical tools such as R and Python to manipulate, analyze, and visualize complex forest and remotely sensed data. Work with standard data structures and formats (Postgres, SQL, Excel, etc.) to clean, organize, and process large datasets. Automate complex processes using R, Python, and other relevant platforms. Integrate geospatial data (e.g., Sentinel-2, LiDAR) into forest planning and/or forest growth models. Collaborate with experienced biometricians and forest planners to address complex forest management challenges. Build creative and effective solutions that drive better decisions in forest inventory, silviculture, harvesting, and growth modeling. Share insights and tools with the team to build collective capacity. Qualifications:Bachelor’s degree in forestry, geospatial sciences, or a related fieldWorking toward a master's degree (or higher) preferred, ideally in biometrics or a quantitative forestry disciplineExperience with forest systems (metrics and silviculture) at a bachelor's level or higherStrong programming skills in R and/or Python (bonus: if you also work in derivatives such as Jupyter Notebooks, or R Shiny)Solid understanding of statistics and quantitative methods. Ability to manage large, messy datasetsFamiliarity with GIS software (QGIS, ESRI), forest growth and yield models (Forest Vegetation Simulator, FVS), or linear programming software (Woodstock Optimization Studio)Strong problem-solving skills and creativity Growth mindsetAbility to work in teams and collaborate with various groups across AFM Professional integrity, someone who does the right thing even when no one is lookingAbility to work both independently and as part of a team Additional Perks:Exposure to complex forest management data and real-world decision-making Opportunity to work with a team of forestry professionals who are passionate about sustainable managementThe chance to make a real impact on how forests are managed Compensation: $18-22 an hour Additional Information: Office Location – Charlotte, NC or remoteAFM will not provide financial assistance with housingFlexible start and end dateThis position is not eligible for employer-sponsored work authorization. jobs.title: Learning & Development Intern at Optimal Care Services LLC
jobs.description: Employer: Optimal Care Services LLC Expires: 10/10/2026 Learning & Development InternshipNew York City Metropolitan AreaPosition SummaryOptimal Care Services (OCS), New York City’s largest provider of Special Education Itinerant Teacher (SEIT) services, is seeking a motivated intern to manage and enhance our Microsoft Viva Learning platform.This is a hands-on role with real ownership. As the Learning & Development Intern, you will maintain OCS’s central training library, organize onboarding and professional development content, track training completion, and help ensure employees can easily access the resources they need.A key project for this internship is supporting the launch of OCS’s new Early Intervention (EI) Division. You will help build the EI learning library, develop onboarding pathways for new staff, and track required training and credentialing requirements. This is a unique opportunity to help create a training program from the ground up while gaining experience in learning management, content organization, and workforce development. Essential Duties and Responsibilities1. Content Curation and Library ManagementOwn the Viva Learning library: build and maintain a clear taxonomy of categories, tags, and collections so a SEIT teacher, a billing specialist, and a new hire each find what they need in under a minute.Source new learning material on an ongoing basis. from Microsoft Learn, LinkedIn Learning, third-party providers, and OCS's own subject-matter experts, and propose additions monthly rather than waiting to be asked.Vet every item before it is published: check accuracy, relevance to preschool special education practice, currency, accessibility, and licensing. Retire content that is outdated, duplicated, or unused.Publish internally developed content — recorded trainings, SOPs, policy walkthroughs, and onboarding materials — into the library with consistent titles, descriptions, thumbnails, and metadata.Maintain a content calendar so the library refreshes on a predictable cadence and seasonal needs (school-year onboarding, annual policy updates, audit season) are met ahead of time.Build the Early Intervention collection from scratch — source, vet, and publish content covering EI program fundamentals, the IFSP process, family-centered and natural-environment practice, and EI documentation standards, working with the EI Division leads to fill gaps as the division grows.2. Learning Paths and AssignmentsBuild role-based learning paths for the roles OCS staffs: SEIT teacher, related-service provider, Early Intervention provider and service coordinator, supervisor, billing and compliance staff, administrative support, sequencing content so each path is a coherent program rather than a list of links.Assign required training to the appropriate departments and cohorts, set realistic due dates, and coordinate with department managers before assignments go out.Track completions and follow up on outstanding assignments through reminders and escalation to managers, keeping the tone supportive and the records clean.Coordinate onboarding paths with the Human Resources Manager so every new hire receives a complete, current first-week learning assignment on their start date.Design the EI Division onboarding path as the division launches; a first-day-ready sequence for new EI hires that no one has built yet and revise it as the program takes shape.3. Compliance Training TrackingMaintain the master schedule for mandated and regulatory training - NYSED, NYC DOE, and NYS DOH requirements, mandated reporter and child abuse identification, workplace harassment prevention, HIPAA and confidentiality, health and safety, and OCS internal policy attestations.Track Early Intervention requirements as a distinct track: training and credentialing tied to New York State Department of Health Bureau of Early Intervention and NYC Early Intervention Program participation, provider approval and renewal dates, and any EI-specific documentation training. Keep this record audit ready from day one rather than reconstructing it later.Track completion status by employee, department, and requirement, and produce audit-ready documentation that stands up to review by NYSED, the NYC DOE, the NYS DOH, or our external auditors.Work with the Compliance Manager on training-related audit requests and on evidence retention: what was assigned, to whom, when it was completed, and where the record is stored.Surface gaps early: flag approaching deadlines, lapsing certifications, and staff who are at risk of falling out of compliance before a deadline is missed.4. Usage Reporting and AdoptionTurn Viva Learning analytics into a monthly dashboard covering active users, completion rates, most- and least-used content, and adoption by department.Report findings to HR leadership with recommendations: what to promote, what to retire, where a path is too long, and where a department needs a nudge.Promote the platform internally through Teams announcements, short how-to guides, and periodic "what's new in the library" communications that staff will open.Gather staff feedback through short surveys and direct outreach and close the loop by acting on what you hear. Qualifications and RequirementsRequiredCurrently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program — education, instructional design, human resources, information systems, library and information science, communications, or a related field.Available for 20–25 hours per week on a consistent weekly schedule during OCS business hours, including at least three days on site.Strong organizational instincts and genuine attention to detail — this role is judged on whether records are accurate and content is where it should be.Comfort with Microsoft 365, particularly Teams, SharePoint, and Excel; ability to learn Viva Learning administration with training and documentation.Clear written communication — you will write content descriptions, staff announcements, and reminder messages that hundreds of employees read.Discretion with confidential employee and training records.PreferredCoursework or experience in instructional design, curriculum development, adult learning, or knowledge management.Familiarity with learning management systems, SCORM content, or digital content curation in any setting.Interest in special education, early childhood, early intervention, or health and human services.Basic comfort with data such as pivot tables and simple dashboards. Success MeasuresAt the end of the first semester, a successful Site Manager will have:a library with a documented taxonomy, no broken or outdated links, and a written content standard others can follow;published learning paths for at least three OCS roles, with onboarding fully covered;a working Early Intervention section — content, onboarding path, and compliance tracker — ready for the division's first cohort of staff;a compliance tracker that gives leadership an accurate completion picture on demand, without a scramble;a monthly usage report with recommendations, and measurable growth in staff engagement with the platform; brought in new material, on their own initiative, that staff use and ask for more of. Compensation and Terms$20.00 per hour, the OCS standard student rate.Paid sick leave in accordance with New York State and New York City law.Academic credit supported where the student's institution permits; OCS will complete required school documentation and supervisor evaluations.Mentorship from the Human Resources Manager and exposure to compliance, finance, and operations leadership.Schedule flexibility around examinations and academic deadlines, arranged in advance. To ApplySubmit a resume and a note describing a time you organized information for other people to use, and one piece of learning content you would add to a library like ours. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Optimal Care Services is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We welcome applicants regardless of economic, linguistic, and cultural differences or physical, learning, and emotional challenges.

jobs.title: Summer 2027 Law Student Internship at Community Legal Aid
jobs.description: Employer: Community Legal Aid Expires: 10/14/2026 Community Legal Aid (CLA) is the civil legal aid program serving the low-income and elderly residents of Central and Western Massachusetts. Through CLA's effective advocacy in more than 8,000 cases each year, some of the most vulnerable residents of the region obtain safe and stable housing; fight discrimination in the housing and employment arenas; access unemployment, disability and other benefits to stabilize their income; break free from domestic violence and other abuse and exploitation; and get needed services in school. In addition, CLA's wholly-owned subsidiary, the Central West Justice Center (CWJC), specializes in cases involving humanitarian-based immigration relief.Community Legal Aid and Affiliate accept law students during the academic year (fall and spring semester) but primarily accept interns for our summer internship program. jobs.description: Employer: Entegris Expires: 10/15/2026 Here at Entegris, we use advanced science to enable technologies that transform the world, and we are seeking employees who have the drive to continue the mission.The Role:Our site in Chaska, MN is seeking a Manufacturing Production Documentation Co-Op to join our team for the Spring 2027 season. We leverage the differences of our employees to bring new ideas to the table. Every employee throughout the company is encouraged to share input on projects and initiatives. Our decision-making process is truly a collaborative effort as we realize there are leaders at every level of the organization. We put our values at the core of how we operate as an organization — not just when it’s convenient, but in a lasting and meaningful way. We want the time and energy you spend here to have a positive impact on your life inside and outside of the office.WHAT WE OFFEROur total rewards package goes above and beyond just a paycheck. Whether you’re looking to build your career, improve your health, or protect your wealth, we offer generous benefits to help you achieve your goals. jobs.title: Appellate Law Clerk at Office of the State Public Defender (CA)
jobs.description: Employer: Office of the State Public Defender (CA) Expires: 10/15/2026 *** You must apply directly at calcareers.ca.gov and submit all required documents as part of the application package to be considered. The job control number is JC-523619. ***Job Description and DutiesThe Office of the State Public Defender (OSPD) has two statutory mandates: representing indigent people on death row in their direct appeals before the California Supreme Court and enhancing the quality and capacity of public defense systems across California. Despite the current execution moratorium, California maintains the largest death row in the Western Hemisphere. To advance the development of the law and improve conditions for our direct representation of indigent people on death row, OSPD also engages in select non-capital appellate representation and amicus work in courts across California.OSPD provides cutting-edge legal services to indigent people convicted of non-capital and capital offenses who appeal their convictions to the California Courts of Appeal and Supreme Court. We are looking to train the next generation of appellate defenders on everything from capital case procedure to how to litigate the Racial Justice Act. As a Summer Appellate Law Clerk with the OSPD Appellate Division, you will become a stronger writer and sharper legal researcher. You will come away with an understanding of what a career in appellate criminal defense entails and a writing sample that will help you open doors. Most importantly, you will be making a difference in the lives of people who need your help.You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement.Working ConditionsOSPD has two regional offices located in Oakland and Sacramento.The Oakland office is located downtown in a modern high-rise building near the 19th Street BART station, not to mention a variety of delicious restaurants.The Sacramento office is located downtown in a modern high-rise building near SacRT Light Rail stations, Downtown Commons, and plenty of shopping.OSPD permits hybrid telework in accordance with government code 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California. During the onboarding and training week, you will be required to report in person to either the OSPD Oakland office or an off-site training location. After the initial training and onboarding week, GSA’s may have either a full-time telework schedule from anywhere in the state, a full-time in-office schedule, or a hybrid schedule, to be agreed upon with their supervisor. Business travel reimbursements consider an employee's designated Headquarters Location, primary residence. The policy may be subject to change by the Department of Human Resources (CalHR). All commute expenses to headquatered location will be the responsibility of the selected candidate.The position may require traveling to clients, conferences, meetings, and training events up to 10% of the time and includes occasional overnight travel, up to a week. Travel is primarily by automobile but also includes occasional train, airplane, or public transportation.Special RequirementsRegistration as a graduate student in law at a college or university of recognized standing. (Persons appointed during the summer months must produce evidence of eligibility for such registration in the following enrollment period.) Required Application Package DocumentsThe following items are required to be submitted with your application. Applicants who do not submit the required items timely may not be considered for this job:Current version of the State Examination/Employment Application STD Form 678 (when not applying electronically), or the Electronic State Employment Application through your Applicant Account at www.CalCareers.ca.gov. All Experience and Education relating to the Minimum Qualifications listed on the Classification Specification should be included to demonstrate how you meet the Minimum Qualifications for the position.Resume is required and must be included.Other - Cover LetterOther - Two Professional ReferencesOther - Education Documents - Law School Transcripts: Official and Non-Official transcripts will be accepted; however, a person(s) appointed for the summer months must produce evidence of enrollment in the fall term and a copy of their official college/university transcripts.Other - Legal Writing Sample - Please see "Legal Writing Sample" section for instructions. Applicants requiring reasonable accommodations for the hiring interview process must request the necessary accommodations if scheduled for a hiring interview. The request should be made at the time of contact to schedule the interview. Questions regarding reasonable accommodations may be directed to the EEO contact listed on this job posting.Desirable QualificationsIn addition to evaluating each candidate's relative ability, as demonstrated by quality and breadth of experience, the following factors will provide the basis for competitively evaluating each candidate:Coursework or experience in: Criminal Law, Criminal Procedure, Constitutional Law, Evidence, and/or The Racial Justice Act.Experience working with system-impacted people and/or indigent individuals.Ability to work independently with supervision, and in a team environment.Ability to develop and maintain good working relations with all levels of staff.Ability to maintain security and confidentiality of privileged information in compliance with applicable laws.Knowledge of computer programs such as Word, other Microsoft Office applications, Adobe, and Westlaw and the ability to use such programs efficiently and effectively.Knowledge of legal research and writing principles.Ability to meet scheduled and last-minute deadlines.Ability to problem-solve and manage time effectively.Ability to meet scheduled and last-minute deadlines.Demonstrated ability to act independently and to use good judgment.Ability to communicate effectively both verbally and in writing.Legal Writing SampleA legal writing sample is required. A writing sample that includes substantive legal analysis and reflects your ability to write as an advocate is preferred. If you do not have such a sample, please submit one that best reflects your ability to write and engage in legal analysis. Your sample should be no longer than 10 pages single-spaced or 20 pages double spaced with 12 pt font. Please include a cover page (which does not count toward the page limit) with your writing sample explaining the circumstances under which it was written and the extent to which it reflects independent or edited work. The writing in your sample should be your own and not be generated using artificial intelligence (AI). If any aspect of your writing sample is the result of AI (research, citations, or writing), please identify and explain the extent of AI use in your cover page.*** Applicants who fail to submit a complete application package, including the required writing sample, will NOT be considered. *** Equal Opportunity EmployerThe State of California is an equal opportunity employer to all, regardless of age, ancestry, color, disability (mental and physical), exercising the right to family care and medical leave, gender, gender expression, gender identity, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, military or veteran status, national origin, political affiliation, race, religious creed, sex (includes pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and related medical conditions), and sexual orientation.It is an objective of the State of California to achieve a drug-free work place. Any applicant for state employment will be expected to behave in accordance with this objective because the use of illegal drugs is inconsistent with the law of the State, the rules governing Civil Service, and the special trust placed in public servants.*** You must apply directly at calcareers.ca.gov and submit all required documents as part of the application package to be considered. The job control number is JC-523619. ***

jobs.title: Summer 2027 Legal Clerk at Wilderness Society, The
jobs.description: Employer: Wilderness Society, The Expires: 10/16/2026 The Wilderness Society (TWS) is seeking two current second-year law students for a paid summer 2027 law clerk position. Open to law students of all backgrounds with a demonstrated commitment to the conservation/environmental movement. The position is part of TWS’s legal team, which focuses on leveraging law and policy to defend and protect important landscapes and wildlands, ensure the benefits of public lands are shared equitably, and strengthen bedrock conservation laws and policies. Application Deadline: Applications will close on 10/9/2026 at 5:00 pm PDT. We hope to fill the positions by December.To Apply: please send a cover letter that describes the unique experiences or perspectives you would bring to TWS, resume, transcript, a short writing sample (no more than 5 pages), and 2-3 references through our online application system (NOT ON HANDSHAKE). Location: This position is available to be done remotely (or in office where there is a TWS office where applicable) in the following states: AK, AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, ID, ME, MD, MT, NV, NM, NY, NC, OH, PA, SC, TX, VA, WA, or WY. About the Organization: The Wilderness Society is a national conservation organization dedicated to protecting America’s wild places since 1935. Our mission is to unite people to protect America’s wild places. Through science, advocacy and partnerships with communities and policymakers, we champion the protection of wilderness, national parks, forests, and other public lands that provide clean air and water, wildlife habitat and the freedom to connect with nature. For more information, visit www.wilderness.org. As an organization, we aspire to be inclusive in the work that we do, and in the kind of organization we are. Internally this means working as a team that listens to different points of view, recognizes the contributions of every employee, and empowers each employee to bring their whole selves to work every day. Externally, this means ensuring that public lands are inclusive and welcoming, so that our shared wildlands can help people and nature to thrive. We are committed to equity throughout our work, which we define as our commitment to realizing the promise of our public lands and ensuring that all can share their universal benefits. We aspire to be campaign-oriented, collaborative, innovative, transparent, and supportive of staff and law clerks – our greatest asset. The Megan Dickie Wilderness Leadership Fund:The position is funded by the Megan Dickie Wilderness Leadership Fund. The fund was created in 2017 to honor and sustain Megan Dickie’s passion for wilderness, dedication to inspiring others to protect wild places, and commitment to expanding the cadre of public lands advocates. Megan was a talented TWS attorney and policy expert who passed away unexpectedly at the age of 35. The fund is designed to provide career-building opportunities for law students of all backgrounds, expanding our reach and shaping new leaders for the future of conservation. Clerkship Overview:The law clerk(s) will join TWS’s legal team and assist with applying public land law and policy to protect and defend important conservation policies and place-based decisions for our shared public lands. The clerk(s) will conduct legal and policy research and analysis that will help advance conservation campaigns and legal strategies. Compensation is $25/hour. This is a full-time position (40 hours/week) for 10 weeks. TWS will reimburse clerks for reasonable business expenses, including travel expenses to visit a TWS office location to meet staff in person and have an opportunity to visit federal public lands. TWS does not reimburse routine commute expenses, however. Ideal candidates will excel at conducting legal and policy research, analyzing complex legal questions, and concisely reporting their findings. It is helpful but not needed to have some familiarity with administrative law, environmental or public lands law, agency rulemaking, and the policies/practices of the executive and legislative branches of government. To Apply: please send a cover letter that describes the unique experiences or perspectives you would bring to TWS, resume, transcript, a short writing sample (no more than 5 pages), and 2-3 references through the online application system (NOT ON HANDSHAKE). Applicants for the summer 2027 legal clerkship are also invited to indicate their interest in a spring 2027 and/or fall 2027 legal externship as part of the application for this position. We will consider the summer 2027 position to be the candidate's first choice of position, unless the candidate clearly indicates otherwise in their job application.

jobs.description: Employer: Procter & Gamble (P&G) Expires: 10/31/2026 Job LocationCINCINNATI GENERAL OFFICES Job DescriptionAre you a curious individual who is passionate about the continuously evolving media landscape? Do you see ads and ask yourself why and how they showed up there? If so come work with us to shape the future of media at P&G. At P&G, we believe that diverse experiences help build strong leaders. Mobility is a key component of many management careers, providing opportunities to grow through different assignments, locations, and business challenges. Candidates should be prepared to consider relocation opportunities throughout their career as business needs and development opportunities arise. P&G now has over 150 media roles in North America and that number is continuing to grow. P&G invented the concept of branding and data-driven brand management and is now connecting and extending that through to media with the establishment of in-house media teams embedded within this organization. Working in media at P&G means being more than just an expert media planner or buyer, it means designing, influencing, and implementing media decisions that are directly in service of business goals. We leverage the best people and capabilities in marketing, analytics and purchasing and connect those with media planning and buying experts to maximize outcomes. We answer questions like: How do we reach as many relevant consumers as possible as effectively as possible at the best cost? Where are consumers spending their time with media today? jobs.title: 2027 Group Benefit Solutions (GBS) Underwriting Summer Internship Program (Overland Park, KS) (94521) at New York Life Insurance Company
jobs.description: Employer: New York Life Insurance Company Expires: 11/17/2026 Role Overview If you’re looking to apply strong analytical and quantitative skills in a collaborative, fast-paced environment, an Underwriting internship in Group Benefit Solutions offers an opportunity to gain hands-on experience while building a strong foundation in insurance underwriting. During this 10-week summer internship, you will learn how underwriters evaluate risk, assess potential customers, and develop pricing recommendations for group insurance solutions. Through formal training, mentorship, networking opportunities, and real-world underwriting assignments, you will gain exposure to the underwriting profession while contributing to meaningful business outcomes that help deliver financial protection and peace of mind to millions of people. What You'll Do Participate in structured training sessions to build a foundational understanding of Group Benefits underwriting principles, products, and risk evaluation. Partner with an experienced underwriter through one-on-one mentorship while engaging with senior leaders and expanding your professional network. Analyze real underwriting cases by assessing risk factors and contributing to pricing decisions that support business growth and profitability. Collaborate with fellow Group Benefit Solutions interns on a summer-long project that strengthens analytical thinking, problem-solving, and teamwork skills. Attend speaker sessions and learning events led by New York Life leaders across Underwriting, Finance, and related business functions to broaden your understanding of the organization. What You'll Bring Rising senior pursuing a bachelor's degree in Risk Management, Economics, Finance, Accounting, Mathematics, Data Analytics, Business Management, or a related field. Strong analytical, quantitative, and critical thinking skills with a high level of comfort working with numbers. Effective written and verbal communication skills with the ability to present ideas clearly. Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Microsoft Excel and Word. Interest in pursuing a career in underwriting and the insurance industry. Customer-focused mindset with strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Preferred Skills Overall GPA of 3.0 or higher. Previous coursework or internship experience related to finance, insurance, risk management, or data analysis. Experience working collaboratively on team-based projects. Demonstrated curiosity, initiative, and commitment to continuous learning. Please apply only to the location you would most prefer. If you are selected for an interview, you'll have the opportunity to discuss your location preferences and any other locations you may be interested in at that time. To be eligible for this program, you must be authorized to work in the U.S. We do not offer any type of employment-based immigration sponsorship for this program. Likewise, this program is not available to those authorized to work under optional practical training (OPT) or curricular practical training (CPT). Curious what it’s like to intern at NYL? Check out #NYLEarlyCareers on LinkedIn!#LI-MW1#GBSCampus

jobs.title: Teach Elementary Students This Summer: MTR Camp Literacy Fellowship at MTR
jobs.description: Employer: MTR - Education Expires: 11/19/2026 KEY DATES AND INFORMATION:Application: Visit MTR Camp Info & Application page to learn more and apply. Applications open October 1st.Deadline: November 18th at 11:59pm CSTFellowship Dates: June 6 - July 2, 2027 in Memphis, TNLocation: Memphis, TN (housing is provided)Benefits: $1500 stipend, housing provided, $300 food stipend & some meals provided, hands-on teaching experience & quality professional developmentThe MTR Camp Literacy Fellowship is a paid summer learning experience designed for undergraduate sophomores and juniors in college who are passionate about equal education. Fellows serve at MTR Camp, where Rising 1st-4th grade students receive literacy instruction in a fun-filled camp experience. Fellows also receive training in the science of reading, gain meaningful experience and the opportunity to teach in under-resourced neighborhoods, and are exposed to gospel-centered community development strategies. During their stay in Memphis, Fellows will also live together in campus housing, receive living and food stipends, and get plentiful opportunities to explore the rich history and culture of Memphis. MTR Camp Literacy Fellowship distinctives:Gain real-world teaching experience as an educator in training with the guidance of MTR staff and a mentor teacherReceive training in effective, research-based teaching and literacy practices.Exposure to MTR’s Residency program.Engage in conversations across racial lines, in deep community, concentrated within a historical and biblical context.Develop Christian Community Education values and practices.$1,500 stipendHousing at a local dormitory is provided.$300 food stipend, dinners provided at college dining hall, and orientation week breakfast and lunch provided.QualificationsMinimum requirements for acceptance to the 2027 MTR Camp Literacy Fellowship:An undergraduate sophomore or junior student enrolled in a four-year college/university. Juniors (rising seniors) are preferred. If you are graduating before June 1, 2027 please consider our residency program. High energy, teachable individuals who are interested in teaching in an under-resourced environment.US Citizenship or Permanent Residency.GPA: 2.75 or above.Be able to work the entire camp employment term of June 6 - July 2, 2027.MTR Camp Info & Application pageComplete an online application that requires a resume, one recommendation, and a brief essay before the November 18th deadline. All supporting documents must be submitted by the deadline. After submitting the written application, some applicants will be moved to the asynchronous video interview stage. Contacts:Paige Gray - MTR Camp Coordinator & Recruiter - paige@memphistr.orgMore About Memphis Teacher Residency Memphis Teacher Residency (MTR) recruits, trains, and supports effective teachers in a Christian context. MTR believes educational inequality is among the greatest social justice and civil rights issues of today. MTR offers 3 ways to get involved in the work of Equal Education: 1 job for college seniors and alumni and 2 paid summer internships/fellowships for current college students.HISTORY MTR has been training teacher residents to serve students in under-resourced neighborhoods of Memphis, TN since 2009. Learn more about our program results at MemphisTR.org/resultsMISSIONChristian Love Expressed in Equal EducationAs a response to the gospel mandate to love our neighbors as ourselves, MTR will partner to provide students in Memphis neighborhoods with the same, or better, quality of education as is available to any student in Memphis by recruiting, training, and supporting effective teachers within a Christian context.VISIONRestored Communities Living with Dignity and in PeaceThe vision of MTR is to use our specific work within education, in partnership with other holistic organizations, to help restore communities so that all individuals can become empowered contributors to our city and people of all races and classes can engage with one another in peace.

jobs.title: Summer 2027 Law Clerk Internship at Huntington Bank
jobs.description: Employer: Huntington Bank Expires: 12/01/2026 Summary:Huntington’s internship programs provide emerging talent with meaningful, hands‑on experience aligned to their area of study. Over the course of the interns’ time at Huntington, they gain exposure to key business functions across all segments of the organization. An intern’s experience should be focused on professional growth, skill development, and practical application of academic learning. Interns participate in a structured series of development opportunities, including interactions with senior leadership and career pathing insights. The experience also includes immersion in Huntington’s award‑winning culture through community involvement and team‑based activities. Internships at Huntington are designed to help students build a strong foundation for future career success while contributing to meaningful business initiatives. Internship Opportunities at Huntington:Huntington offers internship opportunities for students who are currently enrolled in an academic program and seeking practical, hands‑on experience in their field of study. Internships take place during a defined period of time and are available across all business segments. The Legal team is seeking:Rising 3L (Winter 2027 or Spring 2028 grads) may participate in the Enterprise Internship Program, an 11-week, role-aligned experience where students work directly with a manager and team on meaningful business initiatives. In addition to hands-on project work, participants gain exposure to executive leadership, participate in Huntington's innovation project, and build connections that may lead to future full-time opportunities. All interns participate in a variety of developmental and professional activities designed to support learning and exposure to the organization. Program components may include:Experience in day‑to‑day responsibilities related to their assigned teamExposure to broader business functionsA structured schedule of professional development sessionsOpportunities to engage with members of the Executive Leadership TeamDiscussions with senior leaders regarding career paths and Huntington’s business areasA team project focused on applying Huntington’s innovation framework to a business‑relevant problemParticipation in volunteer activities and internal events aligned with Huntington’s culture Legal Internship OverviewThe employment law team is looking for a 3L to assist with legal research, preparing memos, reviewing and interpreting legal documents while supporting attorneys and paralegals as needed. jobs.title: Illinois Legislative Staff Intern (ILSIP Program) at University of Illinois Springfield
jobs.description: Employer: University of Illinois Springfield - Graduate Intern Programs Expires: 04/01/2027 Illinois Legislative Staff Internship (ILSIP)For over 60 years, the Illinois Legislative Staff Intern Program (ILSIP) has provided unique paid internships for keenly interested, deeply motivated and talented individuals to work within state government. With the capitol as both workplace and classroom, ILSIP interns earn $3,300 per month working as professional legislative staff.Funded by the Illinois General Assembly and administered by the University of Illinois Springfield, ILSIP grew out of a desire to provide individuals with diverse experience and backgrounds insight into the legislative process. The program offers interns the opportunities with either one of the 4 legislative staffs (Illinois House Democrats, Illinois House Republicans, Illinois Senate Democrats, or Illinois Senate Republicans), or for the non-partisan legislative support unit, COGFA (Commission on Government Forecasting and Accountability). Interns also participate in an academic seminar during the fall semester, conducted by UIS faculty.The ILSIP experience is intended to broaden the perspective of those planning academic, business or government careers so that they will carry into their chosen fields an understanding of the legislative process and how it relates to their work. In addition to providing interns exposure to the legislative process, the program provides legislative leaders with research and other professional staff assistance.ILSIP interns work full-time for 10 months for a monthly stipend of $3,300, along with a tuition waiver for four (4) graduate credit hours over the course of two (2) semesters and the option for student health insurance paid as a benefit of the program. The program accepts applicants from all academic backgrounds who have completed an undergraduate or advanced degree. Applicants who are pursuing an undergraduate degree must have been awarded the degree prior to starting the internship.All application materials are due by March 15. Qualified candidates will be invited to interview over video conference. Final selections/placements are announced late April to mid-May. Internships begin in the fall semester. For more information, interested students may call the UIS Office of Graduate Intern Programs at 217-206-6158 or visit the ILSIP website at Illinois Legislative Staff Intern Program | University of Illinois Springfield (uis.edu).
